Dünya ise yakın olduğu için bu adı alır: {ar:سميت الدنيا لدنوها, tr:summiyeti'd-dunyâ li-dunuvvihâ, gloss:dünyaya yakınlığından dolayı bu ad verilmiştir, source:"د ن و,B002"}.

Yakın hayatı kalıcı olana tercih edenin vardığı yer, ne hayatın ne de ölümün olduğu bir yerdir.

Kur'an bu cümleyi kelimesi kelimesine başka bir sahnede, Musa'nın karşısındaki sihirbazların ağzından verir. Sihirbazlar secdeye kapanıp Harun'un ve Musa'nın Rabbine iman ettiklerini söyleyince Firavun onları el ve ayaklarını çaprazlama kesmekle tehdit eder ve şöyle der: {ar:وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابًۭا وَأَبْقَىٰ, tr:ve le-ta'lemunne eyyunâ eşeddu azâben ve ebkâ, gloss:hangimizin azabının daha çetin ve daha kalıcı olduğunu bileceksiniz, source:20:71}. +strong	tevrat	paralel	WLC:Gen.3.22	Tree and living forever	The commentary calls the Satanic offer a tree of immortality and an imperishable realm; Genesis says the human might eat from the tree of life and live forever, giving the Eden scene its own guarded version of the desired permanence.

+strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Gen.3.22	חיה, live	Genesis uses the Hebrew life root in its statement that eating from the tree could make the human live forever; this is a direct cognate to يَحْيَىٰ in the commentary's contrast between life and death.

+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.26	Moses looks to the reward	Hebrews explains Moses' choice by his regard for a greater future reward; the commentary likewise ranks the hereafter above the present life and calls it more enduring.

+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.4.14	Water springing to eternal life	Jesus describes water becoming a spring that wells up to eternal life; this connects the commentary's life-giving Paradise water with an image of water whose effect is enduring life.

+medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 16:13	God leads to Hades and raises	Wisdom says God has power over life and death, leads down to Hades and brings up again; this expands the commentary's final claim that God both causes death and gives life.
+medium	tevrat	motif	2 Baruch 51:3-5	Righteous transformed to lasting glory	At resurrection the righteous are changed into splendor and live in an enduring order while the wicked wither; this gives apocalyptic detail to the commentary's contrast between the hereafter and the fate of those who reject it.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.19	Abraham expects resurrection	Hebrews says Abraham reasoned that God could raise Isaac even from the dead; this is a Christian interpretation of the Abraham story that makes concrete the commentary's closing claim that God kills and then gives life.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Phil.1.23	Departing to be with Christ is better	Paul says departure to be with Christ is far better than remaining alive; this states a specific preference for the life beyond the present one, matching the commentary's ranking of hereafter over worldly life.
+medium	incil	yorum_gelenegi	SBLGNT:Mark.9.48	Isaiah's worm applied to Gehenna	Mark places Isaiah's undying worm and unquenched fire in Jesus' warning about Gehenna; the Christian reuse shifts Isaiah's corpse image into a warning about final judgment, while still not saying the condemned themselves are alive.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Tim.6.19	Taking hold of true life	After warning against trust in uncertain riches, Paul urges the rich to lay hold of “the life that is truly life”; this gives a concrete Christian counterpart to the commentary's distinction between mere worldly life and life as real benefit.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.1.10	Life and immortality disclosed	Paul says Christ abolished death and brought life and immortality to light; this offers a Christian counter-image to the condemned person's unrelieved suspension between death and life.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.22.2	Leaves for healing	The Paradise river's tree bears leaves for healing the nations; beside the commentary's water that revives anything it touches, Revelation depicts life-giving restoration extending through the whole blessed scene.
+medium	incil	motif	Gospel of Thomas 19	Paradise trees and no taste of death	The saying describes unchanging trees in Paradise and promises that those who know them will not taste death; this is a concrete apocryphal image of the immortality sought in the commentary's false tree offer, recast as a blessed promise.
+weak	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Deut.30.19	חיים, life	Moses urges Israel to choose life so that they and their offspring may live; the Hebrew life cognate matches the ayah's life vocabulary, though its immediate setting is covenantal survival in the land rather than the commentary's hereafter.
+weak	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.13	Blessed dead rest from labor	Revelation calls those who die in the Lord blessed and says they rest from their labors; this complicates the commentary's negated death/life condition by presenting death as a blessed rest for a different group.
*** End Patch";
